ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total wind output of 10.9 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 1.2 GW, representing 11.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Generation across Scotland remains exceptionally clean, maintaining a Scottish carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh versus 64 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, transmission bottlenecks continue to limit export capability. So far today, 213 MWh of Scottish generation has been turned down through Balancing Mechanism bids at a constraint cost of about £7,055. To replace this curtailed renewable volume, an estimated 40,413 m3 of gas was burned elsewhere across the system, releasing 74 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing today's rate indicates an estimated total yearly cost of £3 million for curtailment. While this reflects a constraint cost of approximately £33/MWh for the curtailed power itself, socialising this expense across total UK electricity consumption equates to an estimated increase of under £0.01/MWh on consumer invoices, demonstrating how network limits drive both carbon emissions and balancing costs.
